pages.lesson:
LESSON: MOVEMENT OF MATERIALS IN AND OUT OF THE CELL

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Living Things and their Environment
Topic 2.2: Movement of Materials in and out of the cell

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Movement of Materials in and out of the cell. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do materials move in and out of a cell?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things
2. explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things
3. appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MOVEMENT OF MATERIALS IN AND OUT OF THE CELL
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Movement of Materials in and out of the cell helps you succeed in INTEGRATED SCIENCE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

KEY FACTS: MOVEMENT OF MATERIALS IN AND OUT OF THE CELL
Study Movement of Materials in and out of the cell like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Observe: Name what you can see/touch about “Movement of Materials in and out of the cell” around your school.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Say why Movement of Materials in and out of the cell matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things. You will use ideas from in your school compound, home, farm, or county.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things.
2. Observe, explain, then apply using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Apply: Describe one safe action you can take related to Movement of Materials in and out of the cell this week.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Movement of Materials in and out of the cell is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Name what you can see/touch about “Movement of Materials in and out of the cell” around your school. (skill: demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things)

Example 2: Say why Movement of Materials in and out of the cell matters for health, safety, or the environment in Kenya. (skill: explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things)

Example 3: Describe one safe action you can take related to Movement of Materials in and out of the cell this week. (skill: appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Movement of Materials in and out of the cell to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.
3. Practise this skill: explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate the importance of diffusion and osmosis in living things.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Movement of Materials in and out of the cell from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Movement of Materials in and out of the cell: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Movement of Materials in and out of the cell?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do materials move in and out of a cell?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Movement of Materials in and out of the cell means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: demonstrate diffusion and osmosis in living things.
5. Be able to: explain the role of diffusion and osmosis in living things.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
